cost.network_during_build: git clone of pypa/packaging and hukkin/tomli

summary.reading: An honest per-task baseline on twelve provably fail-to-pass tasks in real repositories, offline, with the instruction derived from pytest's own failure output. A zero here is the starting number, and it is the first time this project has had one.
summary.what_this_does_not_show: nothing about SWE-bench Pro, Terminal-Bench or OSWorld. These are twelve small single-node bugs in pypa/packaging and hukkin/tomli. It shows what the shipped system does when handed a real failing test and a real checkout -- which is the precondition for any of those benchmarks.

failure_anatomy.note: No patch was attempted on any task. All twelve stopped at the same place: the routed capability declares required inputs that a task statement cannot supply -- output_path, request_spec, repo_root, a bibtex-style `symbol`. The routing was not wrong in spirit (diagnose_and_architect is a plausible reading of 'a test fails'), but the capability cannot act from a test failure.
failure_anatomy.the_structure_of_the_gap: build_goal() asks the model for {"actions":[{"type":"terminal_exec","args":{"command":...}}]}. solve() has no code path that produces that shape: it returns a capability envelope with status, routing, required_inputs and non_claims. So the transport's contract and the model's output contract do not meet, and no amount of routing improvement closes it.
